claims.text: A thin aluminum-rich interlayer should be deposited between the zirconium-alloy substrate and the elemental Cr coating.
Premature failure of the baseline elemental Cr coating is caused by elevated-temperature Cr-Zr interdiffusion.
The aluminum-rich interlayer will oxidize during elevated-temperature exposure to form Al2O3.
The Al2O3 formed within the interlayer will be continuous and dense.
A dense alumina scale will physically and chemically impede atomic migration.
The aluminum-rich interlayer will suppress interdiffusion between Cr and Zr at elevated temperature.
Suppressing Cr-Zr interdiffusion will reduce the formation of brittle intermetallic phases.
Reducing interdiffusion and brittle-phase formation will preserve Cr-coating integrity and adhesion.
Relative to the unmodified Cr-coated baseline, the modified coating will have a significantly narrower Cr-Zr interdiffusion zone.
Relative to the baseline, the modified coating will have improved adhesion.
Relative to the baseline, the modified coating will have improved oxidation and corrosion resistance.
The aluminum-rich interlayer will preserve protection under both normal PWR subcritical-water conditions and accident-relevant high-temperature steam.
Cross-sectional microscopy and EDS mapping can be used to compare the Cr-Zr interdiffusion-zone widths of modified and baseline samples.
Failure to obtain a measurable reduction in interdiffusion or improvement in adhesion and oxidation resistance would falsify the hypothesis.
